f.title: Record and report protocol-defined safety-critical adverse events and lab abnormalities to the sponsor
f.statement: The investigator shall record and document adverse events or laboratory abnormalities that the protocol identifies as critical to the safety evaluation, and report them to the sponsor in line with the reporting requirements and within the periods specified in the protocol.
f.clause: Article 41 Reporting of adverse events and serious adverse events by the investigator to the sponsor
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Safety intake & collection

rows.deadline: Within the periods specified in the protocol
rows.quote: The investigator shall record and document adverse events or laboratory abnormalities identified in the protocol as critical to the safety evaluation and report them to the sponsor in accordance with the reporting requirements and within the periods specified in the protocol.
rows.location: Article 41 Reporting of adverse events and serious adverse events by the investigator to the sponsor
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote names investigator and shall-duty; statement faithful.

f.title: Record all adverse events and report all serious adverse events to the sponsor
f.statement: Unless the protocol provides differently, the investigator shall record and document all adverse events and shall report to the sponsor all serious adverse events occurring to subjects treated by him or her in the clinical trial.
f.clause: Article 41 Reporting of adverse events and serious adverse events by the investigator to the sponsor
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Safety intake & collection

rows.quote: The investigator shall record and document all adverse events, unless the protocol provides differently. The investigator shall report to the sponsor all serious adverse events occurring to subjects treated by him or her in the clinical trial, unless the protocol provides differently.
rows.location: Article 41 Reporting of adverse events and serious adverse events by the investigator to the sponsor
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote names investigator, both duties and the protocol exception.

f.title: Report serious adverse events to the sponsor within 24 hours
f.statement: The investigator shall report serious adverse events to the sponsor without undue delay and not later than 24 hours after obtaining knowledge of the events, unless the protocol provides that, for certain serious adverse events, no immediate reporting is required.
f.clause: Article 41 Reporting of adverse events and serious adverse events by the investigator to the sponsor
f.exceptions: Serious adverse events for which the protocol provides that no immediate reporting is required
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Safety intake & collection

rows.deadline: Without undue delay, not later than 24 hours of the investigator obtaining knowledge of the event
rows.quote: The investigator shall report serious adverse events to the sponsor without undue delay but not later than within 24 hours of obtaining knowledge of the events, unless, for certain serious adverse events, the protocol provides that no immediate reporting is required.
rows.location: Article 41 Reporting of adverse events and serious adverse events by the investigator to the sponsor
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: actor, 24-hour deadline, clock start (knowledge of event) and exception all in quote.

deadline_rule.applies_to: Serious adverse events reported by the investigator to the sponsor, unless the protocol provides that no immediate reporting is required

f.title: Send SAE follow-up reports to the sponsor where relevant
f.statement: Where relevant, the investigator shall send a follow-up report to the sponsor so that the sponsor can assess whether the serious adverse event has an impact on the benefit-risk balance of the clinical trial.
f.clause: Article 41 Reporting of adverse events and serious adverse events by the investigator to the sponsor
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote: Where relevant, the investigator shall send a follow-up report to the sponsor to allow the sponsor to assess whether the serious adverse event has an impact on the benefit-risk balance of the clinical trial.
rows.location: Article 41 Reporting of adverse events and serious adverse events by the investigator to the sponsor
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: 'where relevant' kept; quote proves whole statement.

f.title: Keep detailed records of all adverse events reported by investigators
f.statement: The sponsor shall keep detailed records of all adverse events reported to it by the investigator.
f.clause: Article 41 Reporting of adverse events and serious adverse events by the investigator to the sponsor
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Data integrity & records; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote: The sponsor shall keep detailed records of all adverse events reported to it by the investigator.
rows.location: Article 41 Reporting of adverse events and serious adverse events by the investigator to the sponsor
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: verbatim sponsor shall-duty.

f.title: Report post-trial serious adverse events with suspected causality to the sponsor
f.statement: If the investigator becomes aware, after the end of the clinical trial, of a serious adverse event with a suspected causal relationship to the investigational medicinal product in a subject he or she treated, the investigator shall report it to the sponsor without undue delay.
f.clause: Article 41 Reporting of adverse events and serious adverse events by the investigator to the sponsor
f.applicability: Serious adverse events with suspected causal relationship occurring after the end of the clinical trial
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Safety intake & collection

rows.quote: If the investigator becomes aware of a serious adverse event with a suspected causal relationship to the investigational medicinal product that occurs after the end of the clinical trial in a subject treated by him or her, the investigator shall, without undue delay, report the serious adverse event to the sponsor.
rows.location: Article 41 Reporting of adverse events and serious adverse events by the investigator to the sponsor
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: post-trial trigger, actor and deadline in quote.

f.title: Report SUSARs from the clinical trial electronically to EudraVigilance, including third-country sites
f.statement: The sponsor of a clinical trial performed in at least one Member State shall report electronically and without delay to the database referred to in Article 40(1) all relevant information about all suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions to investigational medicinal products occurring in that clinical trial, whether the SUSAR occurred at a clinical trial site in the Union or in a third country.
f.clause: Article 42 Reporting of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions by the sponsor to the Agency
f.applicability: Clinical trials performed in at least one Member State

rows.quote: The sponsor of a clinical trial performed in at least one Member State shall report electronically and without delay to the database referred to in Article 40(1) all relevant information about the following suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions.: (a) all suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions to investigational medicinal products occurring in that clinical trial, irrespective of whether the suspected unexpected serious adverse reaction has occurred at a clinical trial site in the Union or in a third country;
rows.location: Article 42 Reporting of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions by the sponsor to the Agency
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: statement trimmed: 'EudraVigilance clinical trial database' replaced by the quote's 'database referred to in Article 40(1)'; deadline trimmed to 'Without delay' (42(2) periods are in rows 0010-0012). systems tag EudraVigilance kept as classification (Art 40(1) database is the EudraVigilance module).

f.title: Report SUSARs of the same active substance from third-country-only trials of the sponsor or its group or co-development partner
f.statement: The sponsor shall also report all SUSARs related to the same active substance, regardless of pharmaceutical form, strength or indication investigated, in investigational medicinal products used in the clinical trial, that occur in a clinical trial performed exclusively in a third country, where that trial is sponsored by the same sponsor, or by another sponsor that is part of the same parent company or that develops a medicinal product jointly with the sponsor on the basis of a formal agreement. Providing the investigational medicinal product or safety information to a future potential marketing authorisation holder is not considered joint development.
f.clause: Article 42 Reporting of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions by the sponsor to the Agency
f.applicability: SUSARs from clinical trials performed exclusively in a third country
f.exceptions: Provision of the IMP or safety information to a future potential MAH is not joint development
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Submission operations; Partner & vendor oversight

rows.quote: all suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions related to the same active substance, regardless of pharmaceutical form and strength or indication investigated, in investigational medicinal products used in the clinical trial, occurring in a clinical trial performed exclusively in a third country, if that clinical trial is sponsored: (i) by that sponsor, or (ii) by another sponsor who is either part of the same parent company as the sponsor of the clinical trial, or who develops a medicinal product jointly, on the basis of a formal agreement, with the sponsor of the clinical trial. For this purpose, provision of the investigational medicinal product or information to a future potential marketing authorisation holder on safety matters shall not be considered a joint development; and
rows.location: Article 42 Reporting of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions by the sponsor to the Agency
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: below 90: quote is item (b) without the Art 42(1) lead-in, so actor and modal verb come from the lead-in, not the quote.

f.title: Report SUSARs identified after the end of the clinical trial
f.statement: The sponsor shall report all SUSARs to investigational medicinal products occurring in any subject of the clinical trial that are identified by or come to the attention of the sponsor after the end of the clinical trial.
f.clause: Article 42 Reporting of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions by the sponsor to the Agency
f.applicability: SUSARs identified after the end of the clinical trial

rows.quote: all suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions to investigational medicinal products occurring in any of the subjects of the clinical trial, which are identified by or come to the attention of the sponsor after the end of the clinical trial.
rows.location: Article 42 Reporting of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions by the sponsor to the Agency
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: below 90: quote is item (c) without the Art 42(1) lead-in; actor and modal verb not in the quote.

f.title: Report fatal or life-threatening SUSARs within 7 days
f.statement: For fatal or life-threatening SUSARs, the sponsor shall report to the Agency as soon as possible and in any event not later than seven days after the sponsor became aware of the reaction.
f.clause: Article 42 Reporting of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions by the sponsor to the Agency

rows.deadline: As soon as possible and not later than 7 days after the sponsor became aware of the reaction
rows.quote: (a) in the case of fatal or life-threatening suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions, as soon as possible and in any event not later than seven days after the sponsor became aware of the reaction;
rows.location: Article 42 Reporting of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions by the sponsor to the Agency
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: below 90: quote is item (a) of Art 42(2) without its lead-in; actor/recipient and 'shall' come from the lead-in.

deadline_rule.clock_start: the sponsor became aware of the reaction
deadline_rule.applies_to: Fatal or life-threatening SUSARs, to EudraVigilance (Art 42(2)(a)) (calendar days per Reg 1182/71 Art 3(3))

f.title: Report non-fatal, non-life-threatening SUSARs within 15 days
f.statement: For non-fatal or non-life-threatening SUSARs, the sponsor shall report to the Agency not later than 15 days after the sponsor became aware of the reaction.
f.clause: Article 42 Reporting of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions by the sponsor to the Agency

rows.deadline: Not later than 15 days after the sponsor became aware of the reaction
rows.quote: (b) in the case of non-fatal or non-life-threatening suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions, not later than 15 days after the sponsor became aware of the reaction;
rows.location: Article 42 Reporting of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions by the sponsor to the Agency
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: below 90: item (b) of Art 42(2) quoted without lead-in; 'non-fatal or non-life-threatening' wording kept as source.

deadline_rule.clock_start: the sponsor became aware of the reaction
deadline_rule.applies_to: Non-fatal, non-life-threatening SUSARs, to EudraVigilance (Art 42(2)(b)) (calendar days per Reg 1182/71 Art 3(3))

f.title: Report SUSARs that become fatal or life-threatening within 7 days of awareness of that
f.statement: Where a SUSAR was initially considered non-fatal or non-life-threatening but turns out to be fatal or life-threatening, the sponsor shall report it as soon as possible and in any event not later than seven days after becoming aware of the reaction being fatal or life-threatening.
f.clause: Article 42 Reporting of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions by the sponsor to the Agency
f.applicability: SUSARs upgraded to fatal or life-threatening

rows.deadline: As soon as possible and not later than 7 days after the sponsor became aware of the reaction being fatal or life-threatening
rows.quote: (c) in the case of a suspected unexpected serious adverse reaction which was initially considered to be non-fatal or non-life threatening but which turns out to be fatal or life-threatening, as soon as possible and in any event not later than seven days after the sponsor became aware of the reaction being fatal or life-threatening.
rows.location: Article 42 Reporting of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions by the sponsor to the Agency
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: below 90: item (c) of Art 42(2) quoted without lead-in.

deadline_rule.clock_start: the sponsor became aware of the reaction being fatal or life-threatening
deadline_rule.applies_to: SUSARs initially non-fatal/non-life-threatening that turn out fatal or life-threatening (Art 42(2)(c)) (calendar days per Reg 1182/71 Art 3(3))

f.title: Option to submit an initial incomplete SUSAR report followed by a complete report
f.statement: Where necessary to ensure timely reporting, the sponsor may submit an initial incomplete SUSAR report followed by a complete report, in accordance with section 2.4 of Annex III.
f.clause: Article 42 Reporting of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions by the sponsor to the Agency
f.legal_basis: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Art 42(2); Annex III section 2.4

rows.quote: Where necessary to ensure timely reporting, the sponsor may, in accordance with section 2.4 of Annex III, submit an initial incomplete report followed up by a complete report.
rows.location: Article 42 Reporting of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions by the sponsor to the Agency
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: permission, actor and Annex III 2.4 reference in quote.

f.title: Report SUSARs to the Member State where database reporting is not possible due to lack of resources
f.statement: Where a sponsor, due to a lack of resources, does not have the possibility to report to the database referred to in Article 40(1) and has the agreement of the Member State concerned, it may report the SUSAR to the Member State where the SUSAR occurred.
f.clause: Article 42 Reporting of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions by the sponsor to the Agency
f.applicability: Sponsors lacking resources to report to EudraVigilance
f.exceptions: Requires the agreement of the Member State concerned

rows.quote: Where a sponsor, due to a lack of resources, does not have the possibility to report to the database referred to in Article 40(1) and the sponsor has the agreement of the Member State concerned, it may report to the Member State where the suspected unexpected serious adverse reaction occurred.
rows.location: Article 42 Reporting of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions by the sponsor to the Agency
rows.review_note: Review: statement trimmed: removed the Member State's onward-reporting duty, which is outside the quote and not a sponsor duty. Double-check: statement trimmed: removed '(EudraVigilance)' gloss not in quote; permission and MS-agreement condition proved.

f.title: Submit an annual safety report for each investigational medicinal product
f.statement: For investigational medicinal products other than placebo, the sponsor shall submit annually to the Agency, through the database referred to in Article 40(1), a report on the safety of each investigational medicinal product used in a clinical trial for which it is the sponsor.
f.clause: Article 43 Annual reporting by the sponsor to the Agency
f.processes: Aggregate reporting; Clinical safety monitoring; Submission operations

rows.quote: Regarding investigational medicinal products other than placebo, the sponsor shall submit annually through the database referred to in Article 40(1) to the Agency a report on the safety of each investigational medicinal product used in a clinical trial for which it is the sponsor.
rows.location: Article 43 Annual reporting by the sponsor to the Agency
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: statement trimmed: 'through the EudraVigilance clinical trial database' replaced by quote wording 'through the database referred to in Article 40(1)'.

f.title: Option to submit a single annual safety report for all IMPs in a trial if provided in the protocol
f.statement: In a clinical trial using more than one investigational medicinal product, the sponsor may, if the protocol provides for it, submit a single safety report on all investigational medicinal products used in that trial.
f.clause: Article 43 Annual reporting by the sponsor to the Agency
f.applicability: Clinical trials using more than one IMP
f.exceptions: Only if provided for in the protocol

rows.quote: In the case of a clinical trial involving the use of more than one investigational medicinal product, the sponsor may, if provided for in the protocol, submit a single safety report on all investigational medicinal products used in that clinical trial.
rows.location: Article 43 Annual reporting by the sponsor to the Agency
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: permission and protocol condition in quote.

f.title: Include only aggregate and anonymised data in the annual safety report
f.statement: The annual safety report shall contain only aggregate and anonymised data.
f.clause: Article 43 Annual reporting by the sponsor to the Agency

rows.quote: The annual report referred to in paragraph 1 shall only contain aggregate and anonymised data.
rows.location: Article 43 Annual reporting by the sponsor to the Agency
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: below 90: passive; sponsor inferred from 'annual report referred to in paragraph 1'.

f.title: Annual safety reporting runs from first trial authorisation to the end of the last trial with the IMP
f.statement: The annual safety reporting obligation starts with the first authorisation of a clinical trial under this Regulation and ends with the end of the last clinical trial conducted by the sponsor with the investigational medicinal product.
f.clause: Article 43 Annual reporting by the sponsor to the Agency

rows.deadline: From first authorisation of a clinical trial under the Regulation until the end of the last clinical trial with the IMP
rows.quote: The obligation referred to in paragraph 1 starts with the first authorisation of a clinical trial in accordance with this Regulation. It ends with the end of the last clinical trial conducted by the sponsor with the investigational medicinal product.
rows.location: Article 43 Annual reporting by the sponsor to the Agency
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: below 90: scope/period rule rather than a stand-alone duty; actor inferred from Art 43(1).

f.title: Report auxiliary medicinal product safety under the Directive 2001/83/EC pharmacovigilance rules
f.statement: Safety reporting for auxiliary medicinal products shall be made in accordance with Chapter 3 of Title IX of Directive 2001/83/EC.
f.clause: Article 46 Reporting with regard to auxiliary medicinal products
f.legal_basis: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Art 46; Directive 2001/83/EC Title IX Chapter 3

rows.quote: Safety reporting with regard to auxiliary medicinal products shall be made in accordance with Chapter 3 of Title IX of Directive 2001/83/EC.
rows.location: Article 46 Reporting with regard to auxiliary medicinal products
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: below 90: passive cross-reference duty; actor (sponsor/MAH) inferred; content of the duty lies in Directive 2001/83/EC.

f.title: Notify serious breaches through the EU portal within 7 days
f.statement: The sponsor shall notify the Member States concerned, through the EU portal, of a serious breach of this Regulation or of the version of the protocol applicable at the time of the breach, without undue delay and not later than seven days of becoming aware of the breach. A serious breach is one likely to affect to a significant degree the safety and rights of a subject or the reliability and robustness of the data generated in the trial.
f.clause: Article 52 Reporting of serious breaches
f.processes: Quality system & CAPA; Submission operations; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.deadline: Without undue delay, not later than 7 days of becoming aware of the breach
rows.quote: The sponsor shall notify the Member States concerned about a serious breach of this Regulation or of the version of the protocol applicable at the time of the breach through the EU portal without undue delay but not later than seven days of becoming aware of that breach. 2.   For the purposes of this Article, a ‘serious breach’ means a breach likely to affect to a significant degree the safety and rights of a subject or the reliability and robustness of the data generated in the clinical trial.
rows.location: Article 52 Reporting of serious breaches
rows.review_note: Review: systems label 'EU portal (CTIS)' changed to 'EU portal' (Regulation wording). merged 52(1)+(2) kept (duty with its binding definition); quote extended to cover 52(2) so the definition in the statement is proved. Double-check: duty, portal, 7-day deadline, clock start and binding definition in quote.

deadline_rule.applies_to: Notification of a serious breach to the Member States concerned via the EU portal (Art 52) (calendar days per Reg 1182/71 Art 3(3))

f.title: Notify unexpected events affecting benefit-risk that are not SUSARs within 15 days
f.statement: The sponsor shall notify the Member States concerned, through the EU portal, of all unexpected events that affect the benefit-risk balance of the clinical trial but are not SUSARs under Article 42, without undue delay and no later than 15 days from the date the sponsor became aware of the event.
f.clause: Article 53 Other reporting obligations relevant for subject safety
f.exceptions: Events that are SUSARs are reported under Article 42
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Submission operations; Benefit–risk review

rows.deadline: Without undue delay, no later than 15 days from the date the sponsor became aware of the event
rows.quote: The sponsor shall notify the Member States concerned through the EU portal of all unexpected events which affect the benefit-risk balance of the clinical trial, but are not suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions as referred to in Article 42. That notification shall be made without undue delay but no later than 15 days from the date the sponsor became aware of this event.
rows.location: Article 53 Other reporting obligations relevant for subject safety
rows.review_note: Review: systems label 'EU portal (CTIS)' changed to 'EU portal' (Regulation wording). Double-check: duty, exclusion of SUSARs, 15-day deadline and clock start in quote.

deadline_rule.clock_start: the date the sponsor became aware of this event
deadline_rule.applies_to: Unexpected events affecting the benefit-risk balance that are not SUSARs (Art 53) (calendar days per Reg 1182/71 Art 3(3))

f.title: Submit third-country inspection reports through the EU portal
f.statement: The sponsor shall submit to the Member States concerned, through the EU portal, all inspection reports of third-country authorities concerning the clinical trial, and, when a Member State concerned requests it, a translation of the report or its summary in the official Union language indicated in the request.
f.clause: Article 53 Other reporting obligations relevant for subject safety

rows.quote: The sponsor shall submit to the Member States concerned, through the EU portal, all inspection reports of third country authorities concerning the clinical trial. When requested by a Member State concerned, the sponsor shall submit a translation of the report or of its summary in an official language of the Union indicated in the request.
rows.location: Article 53 Other reporting obligations relevant for subject safety
rows.review_note: Review: systems label 'EU portal (CTIS)' changed to 'EU portal' (Regulation wording). Double-check: both submission and translation duties in quote.

f.title: Take urgent safety measures when an unexpected event is likely to seriously affect benefit-risk
f.statement: Where an unexpected event is likely to seriously affect the benefit-risk balance, the sponsor and the investigator shall take appropriate urgent safety measures to protect the subjects.
f.clause: Article 54 Urgent safety measures
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Risk management & minimisation

rows.quote: Where an unexpected event is likely to seriously affect the benefit-risk balance, the sponsor and the investigator shall take appropriate urgent safety measures to protect the subjects.
rows.location: Article 54 Urgent safety measures
rows.review_note: Review: investigator share: clinical-3 moved from consulted to responsible. Double-check: joint actor and duty verbatim; RACI covers sponsor and investigator shares.

f.title: Notify urgent safety measures through the EU portal within 7 days
f.statement: The sponsor shall notify the Member States concerned, through the EU portal, of the event and the urgent safety measures taken, without undue delay and no later than seven days from the date the measures have been taken. This is without prejudice to Chapters III and VII.
f.clause: Article 54 Urgent safety measures

rows.deadline: Without undue delay, no later than 7 days from the date the measures have been taken
rows.quote: The sponsor shall notify the Member States concerned, through the EU portal, of the event and the measures taken. That notification shall be made without undue delay but no later than seven days from the date the measures have been taken. 3.   This Article is without prejudice to Chapters III and VII.
rows.location: Article 54 Urgent safety measures
rows.review_note: Review: systems label 'EU portal (CTIS)' changed to 'EU portal' (Regulation wording). merged 54(2)+(3) kept; quote extended with 54(3) to prove the 'without prejudice' sentence. Double-check: duty, 7-day deadline from date measures taken, and 54(3) in quote.

deadline_rule.clock_start: the date the measures have been taken
deadline_rule.applies_to: Notification of urgent safety measures and the event (Art 54) (calendar days per Reg 1182/71 Art 3(3))

f.title: Provide the investigator with the investigator's brochure
f.statement: The sponsor shall provide the investigator with the investigator's brochure.
f.clause: Article 55 Investigator's brochure

rows.quote: The sponsor shall provide the investigator with the investigator's brochure.
rows.location: Article 55 Investigator's brochure
rows.review_note: Review: split: quote spanned 55(1) and 55(2); this row keeps 55(1) only; RACI adjusted (clinical-3 distributes to investigator). Double-check: verbatim.

f.title: Update the investigator's brochure with new safety information and review it at least annually
f.statement: The investigator's brochure shall be updated where new and relevant safety information becomes available, and shall be reviewed by the sponsor at least once per year.
f.clause: Article 55 Investigator's brochure

rows.deadline: Review at least once per year; update when new relevant safety information becomes available
rows.quote: The investigator's brochure shall be updated where new and relevant safety information becomes available, and shall be reviewed by the sponsor at least once per year.
rows.location: Article 55 Investigator's brochure
rows.review_note: Review: new row split from 0025 (Art 55(2)). Double-check: below 90: update duty is passive (only the annual review names the sponsor); RACI and deadline wording checked and kept.

f.title: Record and store clinical trial information so it can be accurately reported and verified
f.statement: All clinical trial information shall be recorded, processed, handled and stored by the sponsor or investigator, as applicable, so that it can be accurately reported, interpreted and verified while the confidentiality of records and subjects' personal data remain protected under applicable data protection law.
f.clause: Article 56 Recording, processing, handling and storage of information

rows.quote: All clinical trial information shall be recorded, processed, handled, and stored by the sponsor or investigator, as applicable, in such a way that it can be accurately reported, interpreted and verified while the confidentiality of records and the personal data of the subjects remain protected in accordance with the applicable law on personal data protection.
rows.location: Article 56 Recording, processing, handling and storage of information
rows.review_note: Review: clinical-3 added as responsible for the investigator's share. Double-check: actor 'sponsor or investigator, as applicable' stated in quote.

f.title: Implement technical and organisational measures to protect trial information and personal data
f.statement: Appropriate technical and organisational measures shall be implemented to protect processed information and personal data against unauthorised or unlawful access, disclosure, dissemination, alteration, destruction or accidental loss, in particular where processing involves transmission over a network.
f.clause: Article 56 Recording, processing, handling and storage of information

rows.actor: Sponsor or investigator, as applicable (inferred from Art 56(1))
rows.quote: Appropriate technical and organisational measures shall be implemented to protect information and personal data processed against unauthorised or unlawful access, disclosure, dissemination, alteration, or destruction or accidental loss, in particular where the processing involves the transmission over a network.
rows.location: Article 56 Recording, processing, handling and storage of information
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: below 90: passive; actor is inferred from Art 56(1) and is not in the quote; actor field now marked as inferred.

f.title: Keep a clinical trial master file available and accessible to Member States
f.statement: The sponsor and the investigator shall keep a clinical trial master file which at all times contains the essential documents allowing verification of the conduct of the trial and the quality of the data, taking into account all trial characteristics including whether it is a low-intervention trial; it shall be readily available and directly accessible to the Member States on request.
f.clause: Article 57 Clinical trial master file
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Audit & inspection readiness

rows.quote: The sponsor and the investigator shall keep a clinical trial master file. The clinical trial master file shall at all times contain the essential documents relating to that clinical trial which allow verification of the conduct of a clinical trial and the quality of the data generated, taking into account all characteristics of the clinical trial, including in particular whether the clinical trial is a low-intervention clinical trial. It shall be readily available, and directly accessible upon request, to the Member States.
rows.location: Article 57 Clinical trial master file
rows.review_note: Review: clinical-3 added as responsible for the investigator's share. Double-check: actor, content and availability duty in quote.

f.title: Sponsor and investigator master files may differ in content where justified
f.statement: The clinical trial master file kept by the investigator and that kept by the sponsor may have different content if justified by the different nature of their responsibilities.
f.clause: Article 57 Clinical trial master file

rows.quote: The clinical trial master file kept by the investigator and that kept by the sponsor may have a different content if this is justified by the different nature of the responsibilities of the investigator and the sponsor.
rows.location: Article 57 Clinical trial master file
rows.review_note: Review: clinical-3 added as responsible for the investigator's share. Double-check: permission and justification condition in quote.

f.title: Archive the clinical trial master file for at least 25 years after the end of the trial
f.statement: Unless other Union law requires a longer period, the sponsor and the investigator shall archive the content of the clinical trial master file for at least 25 years after the end of the clinical trial, in a way that keeps it readily available and accessible to competent authorities on request. Subjects' medical files are archived in accordance with national law.
f.clause: Article 58 Archiving of the clinical trial master file
f.exceptions: Longer period if other Union law requires; subjects' medical files follow national law

rows.deadline: At least 25 years after the end of the clinical trial
rows.quote: Unless other Union law requires archiving for a longer period, the sponsor and the investigator shall archive the content of the clinical trial master file for at least 25 years after the end of the clinical trial. However, the medical files of subjects shall be archived in accordance with national law. The content of the clinical trial master file shall be archived in a way that ensures that it is readily available and accessible, upon request, to the competent authorities.
rows.location: Article 58 Archiving of the clinical trial master file
rows.review_note: Review: clinical-3 added as responsible for the investigator's share. Double-check: actor, 25-year period, Union-law and national-law qualifications in quote.

f.title: Document transfers of ownership of the clinical trial master file content
f.statement: Any transfer of ownership of the content of the clinical trial master file shall be documented, and the new owner shall assume the archiving responsibilities set out in Article 58.
f.clause: Article 58 Archiving of the clinical trial master file

rows.actor: Party transferring ownership (sponsor or investigator, inferred) to document; new owner to assume Article 58 responsibilities
rows.quote: Any transfer of ownership of the content of the clinical trial master file shall be documented. The new owner shall assume the responsibilities set out in this Article.
rows.location: Article 58 Archiving of the clinical trial master file
rows.review_note: Review: split: archive custodian, archive media and new traceability duty moved to separate rows; actor widened since the transfer sentence is not limited to the sponsor. clinical-3 added as responsible (investigator share). Double-check: below 90: documenting the transfer is passive with no named actor; the reviewer's widening to 'any new owner' is only proved for the second sentence. Actor reworded to separate the inferred transferring party from the quoted new owner.

f.title: List significant RSI changes in the annual safety report and append the revised RSI
f.statement: If there are significant changes to the RSI during the reporting period, they shall be listed in the annual safety report and the revised RSI shall be submitted as an appendix in addition to the RSI in effect at the start of the period; the RSI in effect at the start of the period still serves as RSI during the period.
f.clause: Annex III Safety reporting, 3. Annual safety reporting by the sponsor, point 25

rows.quote: If there are significant changes to the RSI during the reporting period they shall be listed in the annual safety report. Moreover, in this case the revised RSI shall be submitted as an appendix to the report, in addition to the RSI in effect at the start of the reporting period. Despite the change to the RSI, the RSI in effect at the start of the reporting period serves as RSI during the reporting period.
